subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Crossover Craze
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Crossover Craze.

hook.text: Crossovers barely existed in 2005. Now they dominate car sales in almost every country.

buildup.text: A crossover is basically a tall hatchback—built on a car platform but styled like a small SUV.

discovery.text: Buyers love the high seating position, easy entry, and cargo space without true SUV bulk.

twist.text: Most crossovers never go off-road. The rugged look is largely cosmetic.

climax.text: Sedans, coupes, and wagons are disappearing as automakers pour resources into crossovers instead.

punchline.text: The crossover won by being good enough at everything.

quiz.question: What is a crossover built on?

details.summary: Crossover SUVs combining car-like handling with SUV practicality became the best-selling vehicle type worldwide by the 2010s, overtaking sedans as the default family car choice.
details.whyItMatters: The crossover craze redefined what a mainstream car looks like. Automakers shifted billions in investment from sedans to crossovers, reshaping product lines globally.
takeaways: Crossovers sit on car platforms rather than truck frames
They offer higher seating, cargo space, and all-wheel drive
Sedan sales dropped sharply as crossovers dominated showrooms

faq.question: What's the difference between a crossover and a real SUV?
faq.answer: Traditional SUVs use a truck-based body-on-frame platform designed for off-road capability. Crossovers use a car-based unibody platform that is lighter, more fuel-efficient, and better to drive on pavement.

faq.question: Why did consumers abandon sedans for crossovers?
faq.answer: Crossovers offer a higher driving position, easier entry, more cargo flexibility, and available all-wheel drive. Their fuel economy improved to near-sedan levels, removing the last reason to choose a sedan.
